log.why: Knocking out {hisG, dnaK} splits the prior mass nearly evenly (0.473 vs 0.527), maximizing information gain on the more urgent ticket.
Treating at 10 uM splits Ticket 2's probability mass nearly evenly (0.439 vs 0.561) while Ticket 1 incubates.
Testing lacZ directly splits the posterior roughly in half and confirms the leading candidate if the phenotype is lost.
Treating at 3 uM evenly splits the posterior (0.453 vs 0.547) and strongly tests the leading 10 uM hypothesis.
Testing top candidate rpoB directly on the most urgent ticket can confirm it for immediate publication or narrow the field to gyrA.
Testing 1 µM cleanly separates the leading 3 µM hypothesis from lower thresholds before publishing.
Testing 0.3 µM splits the lower thresholds from the leading 1 µM hypothesis while utilizing a free incubator before publishing Ticket 1.
Testing {ompF, lacZ} splits Ticket 3's prior nearly in half (0.44) and incubates while we publish Ticket 1 next.
With only 4 seconds left and strong evidence for rpoB (0.867 posterior from E4 phenotype loss), we must publish immediately before expiration.
With 10s left there is no time for another plate, and 0.533 posterior gives positive expected value over expiration.
Ticket 3 expires soon; testing trpE cleanly separates the top two candidates (trpE and gyrA) before publishing.
Run E5 on Ticket 4 to split the prior nearly evenly (0.40 vs 0.60) while waiting 6 s for Ticket 3's E1.
Ticket 4 has 27s left; knocking out lacZ cleanly resolves the top two candidates, lacZ and ompF, before publishing.
E8 bisects the posterior (0.492 vs 0.508), either boosting katG above 0.62 or isolating gyrA and trpE for one decisive follow-up.
Testing 30 µM on Ticket 5 separates <=30 µM from >=100 µM while leaving time for another experiment and two publications.
With 14s left in the round, publishing katG (0.622 posterior) has high expected value and finishes just before Ticket 5's plate reads.
